mistakes.quizTitle: AZ-104 — Describe Azure Identity, Access, and Security Quiz
mistakes.question: Which passwordless options does Microsoft Entra ID support? (Choose three)
options: Windows Hello for Business
Microsoft Authenticator app
FIDO2 security keys
Microsoft Entra Connect sync
mistakes.explanation: Entra ID supports three passwordless options: Windows Hello for Business, the Microsoft Authenticator app, and FIDO2 security keys.

mistakes.quizTitle: AZ-104 — Describe Azure Identity, Access, and Security Quiz
mistakes.question: How are B2B collaboration users represented in your directory?
options: As guest users in your directory
As full member accounts in your directory
They aren't in your directory at all
As managed identities on your resources
mistakes.explanation: B2B collaboration users are represented in your directory, typically as guest users.

mistakes.quizTitle: AZ-104 — Describe Azure Identity, Access, and Security Quiz
mistakes.question: What does B2B direct connect currently support, and how are its users represented?
options: Teams shared channels; users aren't in your directory
SaaS app publishing; users appear as guests
Domain join; users appear as members
LDAP queries; users sync to the managed domain
mistakes.explanation: B2B direct connect supports Teams shared channels; those users aren't represented in your directory but are visible in the shared channel and Teams admin center reports.

mistakes.quizTitle: AZ-104 — Describe Azure Identity, Access, and Security Quiz
mistakes.question: How does Zero Trust change the traditional perimeter model?
options: Access is based on authentication and risk, not network location
Access depends only on being inside the corporate network
VPN access grants full internal trust by default
Personal devices are always blocked from any access
mistakes.explanation: Zero Trust grants access based on authentication and context (identity, device, risk) rather than assuming safety from network location.

mistakes.quizTitle: AZ-104 — Describe Azure Identity, Access, and Security Quiz
mistakes.question: Which layer uses DDoS protection and perimeter firewalls?
options: The perimeter layer
The data layer
The compute layer
The identity and access layer
mistakes.explanation: The perimeter layer uses DDoS protection to filter large-scale attacks and perimeter firewalls to identify and alert on malicious attacks.

mistakes.quizTitle: AZ-104 — Describe Azure Identity, Access, and Security Quiz
mistakes.section: Defender for Cloud Hybrid and Multicloud
mistakes.question: What is required to extend Defender for Cloud protection to non-Azure machines?
options: Deploy Azure Arc and enable enhanced security features
Deploy Microsoft Entra Connect to those machines
Move the machines into a managed domain
Enable single sign-on on each machine
mistakes.explanation: Azure Arc can extend Microsoft Defender plans to non-Azure machines; deploy Arc and enable Defender for Cloud's enhanced security features.

mistakes.quizTitle: AZ-104 — Describe Azure Identity, Access, and Security Quiz
mistakes.question: What are the three vital functions Defender for Cloud fills? (Choose three)
options: Continuously assess
Secure
Defend
Synchronize
mistakes.explanation: Defender for Cloud continuously assesses posture, secures resources with the Microsoft cloud security benchmark (MCSB), and defends against threats.

mistakes.quizTitle: AZ-104 — Describe Azure Identity, Access, and Security Quiz
mistakes.question: Which protections are part of Defender for Cloud's advanced threat protection?
options: Just-in-time VM access and adaptive application controls
Domain join and group policy management
Self-service password reset and smart lockout
One-way synchronization to a managed domain
mistakes.explanation: Advanced threat protection includes just-in-time VM access and adaptive application controls for resources like VMs, SQL, containers, and networks.

mistakes.quizTitle: AZ-104 — Understand Microsoft Entra ID Quiz
mistakes.question: How does implementing Microsoft Entra ID compare to deploying AD DS domain controllers on Azure virtual machines?
options: They're different services — neither involves deploying or relying on the other's domain controllers.
They're functionally identical because both install the exact same underlying directory service software.
Microsoft Entra ID is a managed wrapper around AD DS controllers on Azure VMs.
Microsoft Entra ID automatically deploys the domain controllers needed for an on-premises forest.
mistakes.explanation: The module explicitly treats these as different, unrelated services — Entra ID isn't a wrapper around VM-hosted domain controllers, and it doesn't deploy any domain controllers itself.

mistakes.quizTitle: AZ-104 — Understand Microsoft Entra ID Quiz
mistakes.question: From a technical standpoint, what does the term tenant represent?
options: An individual Microsoft Entra service instance, technically speaking.
A single Azure subscription, regardless of how many directories it uses.
A specific resource group used to organize identity-related resources.
A network boundary defined by a virtual network's address space.
mistakes.explanation: Technically, a tenant is an individual Microsoft Entra instance — not a subscription, a resource group, or a network boundary.

mistakes.quizTitle: AZ-104 — Understand Microsoft Entra ID Quiz
mistakes.question: What's true about adding a custom domain name to a Microsoft Entra tenant alongside its default onmicrosoft.com domain?
options: A custom domain using the organization's own DNS namespace can be added too.
Custom domains can replace the default domain, but the two can never coexist.
Custom domains require a separate Microsoft Entra tenant to be created first.
Custom domains are available with the Premium P2 tier, never with Free.
mistakes.explanation: Adding a custom domain alongside the default one is described as possible and common — it doesn't replace the default, require a new tenant, or need the P2 tier.

mistakes.quizTitle: AZ-104 — Understand Microsoft Entra ID Quiz
mistakes.question: What does the module say about extending the Microsoft Entra schema?
options: It's easily extensible, and its extensions are fully reversible.
It can be extended, but extensions can never be reversed once applied.
It can't be extended under any circumstances, unlike the AD DS schema.
It can be extended by Microsoft support engineers, not by customers.
mistakes.explanation: The schema is described as easily extensible with fully reversible extensions — not irreversible, non-extensible, or support-engineer-only.

mistakes.quizTitle: AZ-104 — Understand Microsoft Entra ID Quiz
mistakes.question: Since Microsoft Entra ID doesn't include the organizational unit (OU) class, how can administrators achieve a similar arrangement of objects?
options: By organizing objects based on their group membership.
By creating nested resource groups that mirror an OU hierarchy.
By assigning each object to a separate Azure subscription.
By using Conditional Access policies to simulate an OU structure.
mistakes.explanation: Group membership is the suggested equivalent arrangement — not nested resource groups, separate subscriptions, or Conditional Access policies.

mistakes.quizTitle: AZ-104 — Understand Microsoft Entra ID Quiz
mistakes.question: What is the relationship between the Application class and the servicePrincipal class in Microsoft Entra ID?
options: An Application object holds the definition; a servicePrincipal is its instance in a tenant.
A servicePrincipal holds the app's definition; an Application represents its instance in a tenant.
Application and servicePrincipal are two names for the exact same object, used interchangeably.
Application objects exist in AD DS, while servicePrincipal objects exist in Microsoft Entra ID.
mistakes.explanation: Application holds the definition and servicePrincipal is its per-tenant instance — the roles aren't reversed, identical, or split across AD DS and Entra ID.

mistakes.quizTitle: AZ-104 — Understand Microsoft Entra ID Quiz
mistakes.question: Why does separating an application's definition from its servicePrincipal matter for multi-tenant scenarios?
options: Defining an app once lets you reuse it across tenants via a service principal in each.
It lets a single servicePrincipal object be shared and reused identically across every tenant.
It removes the need to register the application in any tenant before it can be used.
It allows the application's definition to be edited independently in every tenant where it's used.
mistakes.explanation: This separation allows one definition to be reused across tenants via a service principal per tenant — service principals aren't shared as one object, registration is still required, and the definition isn't independently editable per tenant.

mistakes.quizTitle: AZ-104 — Understand Microsoft Entra ID Quiz
mistakes.section: Comparing AD DS and Microsoft Entra ID
mistakes.question: Which of the following is a stated characteristic of AD DS?
options: It's a true directory service with a hierarchical X.500-based structure.
It's accessed exclusively through a REST API over an HTTPS connection endpoint.
It primarily uses OAuth and OpenID Connect tokens for its authentication.
It's natively multi-tenant, isolating each company's data automatically by design.
mistakes.explanation: AD DS has a hierarchical X.500-based structure — REST API access, OAuth/OpenID Connect, and native multi-tenancy are Entra ID characteristics instead.

mistakes.quizTitle: AZ-104 — Understand Microsoft Entra ID Quiz
mistakes.section: Microsoft Entra ID for Cloud Apps
mistakes.question: Besides Microsoft cloud services, which other kinds of applications can Microsoft Entra ID provide an SSO experience for, according to this module?
options: Applications such as Facebook, Google services, and Yahoo.
Applications hosted on AD DS-joined virtual machines alone.
Applications published through the Azure Marketplace catalog.
Applications built using the Microsoft Identity Manager SDK.
mistakes.explanation: Facebook, Google services, and Yahoo are named as SSO-capable third parties — Entra ID's SSO isn't limited to AD DS-joined VMs, Marketplace apps, or MIM SDK-built apps.

mistakes.quizTitle: AZ-104 — Understand Microsoft Entra ID Quiz
mistakes.section: Microsoft Entra ID for Cloud Apps
mistakes.question: What's true about Microsoft Entra authentication settings across the deployment slots of a single Web App?
options: Different authentication settings can be applied to individual deployment slots.
All deployment slots are required to share identical authentication settings.
Authentication settings can be changed for the production slot alone.
Authentication settings for slots are managed entirely outside the Azure portal.
mistakes.explanation: Per-slot authentication settings are explicitly supported — slots aren't forced to share identical settings, restricted to production-only changes, or managed outside the portal.

mistakes.quizTitle: AZ-104 — Understand Microsoft Entra ID Quiz
mistakes.section: Microsoft Entra ID P1 and P2 Plans
mistakes.question: Which Microsoft Entra ID P1 feature lets end users request to join groups while group owners approve membership?
options: Self-service group management.
Conditional Access.
Identity Protection.
Privileged Identity Management.
mistakes.explanation: Self-service group management covers this workflow — Conditional Access, Identity Protection, and Privileged Identity Management serve different purposes.

mistakes.quizTitle: AZ-104 — Understand Microsoft Entra ID Quiz
mistakes.section: Microsoft Entra ID P1 and P2 Plans
mistakes.question: What is distinctive about the advanced security reports and alerts included in Microsoft Entra ID P1?
options: They're machine learning based and highlight anomalies and inconsistent access patterns.
They're generated manually by Microsoft support on a quarterly basis.
They cover sign-ins that originate from non-browser applications alone.
They're available exclusively to Enterprise Admins, not to standard administrators.
mistakes.explanation: They're machine learning based, surfacing anomalies and inconsistent access patterns — not manually produced, non-browser-only, or restricted to Enterprise Admins.

mistakes.quizTitle: AZ-104 — Understand Microsoft Entra ID Quiz
mistakes.section: Microsoft Entra ID P1 and P2 Plans
mistakes.question: What does the Cloud App Discovery feature of Microsoft Entra ID P1 do?
options: It discovers the most frequently used cloud-based applications.
It automatically blocks any cloud application not on an approved allow-list.
It migrates discovered cloud applications into Microsoft Entra Domain Services.
It generates a complete network topology diagram of on-premises infrastructure.
mistakes.explanation: Cloud App Discovery surfaces frequently used cloud apps — it doesn't block apps, migrate them into Entra Domain Services, or map on-premises network topology.

mistakes.quizTitle: AZ-104 — Understand Microsoft Entra ID Quiz
mistakes.question: What problem does Microsoft Entra Domain Services primarily address?
options: Authenticating line-of-business apps in Azure without a VPN or DCs.
Replacing Microsoft Entra ID entirely as the organization's primary cloud identity provider.
Eliminating the need for any Microsoft Entra tenant to exist at all.
Providing a graphical reporting dashboard for AD DS replication network traffic.
mistakes.explanation: It's positioned as an alternative to a site-to-site VPN or replica domain controllers for authenticating migrated apps — it doesn't replace Entra ID, remove the need for a tenant, or just report on replication.

mistakes.quizTitle: AZ-104 — Understand Microsoft Entra ID Quiz
mistakes.question: What domain-related capabilities does Microsoft Entra Domain Services provide?
options: Group Policy management, domain joining, and Kerberos authentication.
LDAP schema replication and trust relationships between forests.
Computer object provisioning identical to a full AD DS deployment.
Native support for nested organizational units across domains.
mistakes.explanation: GPO management, domain joining, and Kerberos authentication are the stated capabilities — forest trusts, full AD DS-equivalent computer objects, and nested OUs aren't part of this service.

mistakes.quizTitle: AZ-104 — Understand Microsoft Entra ID Quiz
mistakes.question: What's true about using Microsoft Entra Domain Services without any on-premises AD DS deployed?
options: It works as a cloud service with no on-premises AD DS.
It needs at least one on-premises domain controller running to function.
It can operate as an extension of an existing AD DS forest.
It needs Microsoft Entra Connect installed locally first before it starts.
mistakes.explanation: It can run entirely cloud-only with no on-premises AD DS — it doesn't require a local domain controller, an existing forest, or a local Entra Connect install.

mistakes.quizTitle: AZ-104 — Understand Microsoft Entra ID Quiz
mistakes.question: How is Microsoft Entra Domain Services billed?
options: Per hour, based on the size of the directory.
A flat monthly fee, regardless of directory size.
Per authentication request that gets processed each time.
It's included at no extra cost with any Microsoft Entra tenant.
mistakes.explanation: Billing is per hour based on directory size — not a flat monthly fee, per-request billing, or a free inclusion with any tenant.

mistakes.quizTitle: AZ-104 — Understand Microsoft Entra ID Practice Assessment
mistakes.question: An organization wants to grant administrators temporary, time-bound elevated privileges that activate through an approval workflow rather than being permanently assigned. Which feature should they use?
options: Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management.
Conditional Access, evaluated by device or location signals.
Microsoft Entra ID Protection, for sign-in risk.
Microsoft Identity Manager licensing, for hybrid identity stores.
mistakes.explanation: Privileged Identity Management defines permanent and temporary administrators with an activation workflow — Conditional Access, Identity Protection, and MIM serve different purposes.

mistakes.quizTitle: AZ-104 — Understand Microsoft Entra ID Practice Assessment
mistakes.question: An organization is moving line-of-business apps that rely on domain-joined authentication to Azure, and wants to avoid deploying or managing any domain controllers in the cloud. Which complete solution addresses this requirement?
options: Microsoft Entra Domain Services, used as the complete fix.
A site-to-site VPN between the local infrastructure and Azure IaaS.
Replica domain controllers deployed as Azure VMs from the local AD DS.
Microsoft Entra ID alone, without enabling any additional service.
mistakes.explanation: Entra Domain Services is presented as the alternative that avoids deploying or managing cloud domain controllers — a site-to-site VPN and replica domain controllers are the two approaches it's meant to replace, and Entra ID alone doesn't provide domain join or Kerberos authentication for these apps.
